author: sjm41
body:
* **PTHR ID & PTN node:**
PTN000467663 (PTN008573477)

* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
Fly CG42258 (FBgn0259143)

* **Type of Issue: Erroneous source or erroneous propagation, or other issue**
erroneous propagation

CG42258 is annotated with enables histone acetyltransferase activity (GO:0004402) IBA with [PANTHER:PTN000467663]

The 2 sources for that annotation are:
fly Atac2 (FlyBase=FBgn0032691|UniProtKB=Q9VJ73)
fly KAT14 (HGNC=15904|UniProtKB=Q9H8E8)
These are clear orthologs of each other.

But I don't see the relationship between CG42258 and Atac2/KAT14.
In FlyBase, at least, we list no paralogs of CG42258 and no human orthologs of CG42258. It also has zero domains annotated by InterPro.

If you can see a good reason for grouping CG42258 with Atac2/KAT14, and giving it the histone acetyltransferase annotation, please let me know!
Otherwise, maybe we can drop the propagation to CG42258?
title: PTN000467663 (PTN008573477)

author: marcfeuermann
body:
I've blocked the annotation for CG42258.
This was due to the fact that, within the phylogenetic tree, the 2 drosophila proteins cluster together (see figure below). 
So there is maybe a problem with the tree topology. Several other cases have been spotted. I will send them all to our PANTHER colleagues for further investigation.
Thanks.
